structured.answer: I'd open the account at Pesagot and buy the "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125" fund (5112628). The page marks that pair "★ הזול" and says it leaves the most, about 86,045 ₪ after 10 years. That's for the page's own example of 10,000 ₪ now plus 500 a month, though, not my 30,000, and I couldn't move the fields to check.

stuck.where: Top calculator, סכום היום / הפקדה חודשית
stuck.why: It was already set to 10,000 and 500. My amount is 30,000 and I couldn't get it there, so every number after that is for someone else's money.

stuck.where: Fund list, the -0.04%, -0.37%, -0.54% under each fund
stuck.why: Minus signs next to every fund. At first I read that as each fund losing money. Only the bottom note "מול המדד" hints it means behind the index, and I didn't really read it.
Leumi is the name I know and trust. Pesagot is the cheapest, but I had to think about whether I trust it. In the end the star and the 'most money' line decided it.
Only about 16,000 more after 10 years at 7%? I expected more, something like +70%. Maybe it's because of 'בכסף של היום', but I'm not sure.

findings.what: Every fund has a minus percent in red-ish purple. It looks like they all lose money, which scares me off, and the explanation is buried in grey text at the bottom
The calculator starts at 10,000 and 500, so the big 86,045 ₪ that sticks in my head isn't my number
After 10 years at 7% it shows only ~16,000 above what I put in. Nothing near the top explains that it's 'in today's money' after tax, so it feels wrong
Lots of fee words (דמי משמרת, נאמן, העמלות זו על זו) in a colour bar. I don't know which one matters
The cheapest account is not the bank I know. It's never said why I should trust it
The last chart starts at a different answer (הראל, ירושלים 79,910) than the one picked above, which confused me
No clear 'next step' button to actually open the account or buy
